evals.name: survival-hud-and-pause
evals.prompt: I'm making a top-down survival shooter in Godot 4. I need a HUD that shows health, ammo and the current wave number, and a pause menu with a volume slider. Right now there's no UI at all. Can you build it?
evals.expected_output: Working .gd files in the project that compile under Godot 4, giving a HUD with three readouts and a functioning pause menu.
assertions: The project compiles under Godot 4.7: an --import pass produces no SCRIPT ERROR, Parse Error, Failed to load script or Compilation failed.
The HUD shows all three requested readouts: health, ammo, and wave number.
A pause menu exists and contains a volume slider.
Every node in the pause overlay sets process_mode to PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, so its buttons still respond while get_tree().paused is true.
HUD text is given BOTH a font outline and a drop shadow, so it stays readable over arbitrary gameplay.
The UI requires no image or font asset files (no .png/.svg/.ttf referenced or needed).

evals.name: reskin-programmer-art
evals.prompt: My Godot 4 roguelike's UI is embarrassing - it's just plain white Labels sitting on default grey Panels, no styling at all. I want it to actually look designed. The game is dark fantasy, lots of deep purples and bone white. Can you sort out the look of the HUD?
evals.expected_output: A themed UI with a coherent dark-fantasy palette, styled panels and readable text over gameplay.
assertions: The project compiles under Godot 4.7: an --import pass produces no SCRIPT ERROR, Parse Error, Failed to load script or Compilation failed.

Colours are defined once in a single central theme/palette location rather than scattered as literals across screen scripts. Judge this the way scripts/palette_lint.py does: no Color(...) literal with a hue outside the theme file, and no literal anywhere that merely repeats a palette constant's value - both render correctly today and survive a re-skin, which is the defect. Achromatic literals (black, white, grey) are fine.
The palette matches the brief: deep purples and a bone-white text colour.
Panels use StyleBoxFlat with corner radii and borders rather than Godot's default grey Panel styling.
HUD text is given BOTH a font outline and a drop shadow, so it stays readable over arbitrary gameplay.
The UI requires no image or font asset files (no .png/.svg/.ttf referenced or needed).

evals.name: results-screen-collection
evals.prompt: Add a level-complete screen to my Godot 4 puzzle game. It should show the time taken and the number of moves used, and also a grid of all 30 collectible stamps in the game with the ones the player has found highlighted and the rest greyed out.
evals.expected_output: A results screen script showing stat readouts plus a collection grid where unfound entries remain visible but blanked.
assertions: The project compiles under Godot 4.7: an --import pass produces no SCRIPT ERROR, Parse Error, Failed to load script or Compilation failed.
The screen displays both the time taken and the number of moves used.
The collection grid contains all 30 stamp entries, not only the found ones.
Unfound stamps remain visible as blanked/greyed cells rather than being omitted from the grid.
The screen is driven by data passed in (a present()-style call or exported arrays) rather than 30 hard-coded nodes.
The UI requires no image or font asset files (no .png/.svg/.ttf referenced or needed).
